info.description:
**trixd** is the TrinityX daemon for everything that is not a physical node: the cluster's users and groups, the Prometheus monitoring configuration, starting and stopping services, and the slurm and genders files computed from Luna's node list. Every route below says what it does, what to send, what comes back, and who may call it.

**Luna**, luna2-daemon, runs beside it on this controller and owns the physical estate: nodes, groups, images, networks and boot. It answers at https://<controller>:7050, and [https://<controller>:7050/version](https://<controller>:7050/version) says which version it runs. A request to `/api/v1/luna/<path>` here is handed to Luna as `/<path>`, unchanged, and Luna decides who may.

### Signing in
1. `POST /api/v1/auth/token` with `{"username": "...", "password": "..."}` answers `201` and `{"token": "..."}`, valid for an hour unless `trixd.ini` says otherwise.
2. Send the token on every call as `x-access-tokens: <token>`, as Luna takes it, or as `Authorization: Bearer <token>`.
3. On this page: **Authorize**, paste the token into either field, and every **Try it out** sends it.

### Who may call what
A user holds one role: `none` < `reader` < `operator` < `manager`. Each route admits a lowest role, shown as **Access** under its description. **rootus**, the account `trixd.ini` names, is the administrator and passes every check. `none` may only ask who it is, with `GET /api/v1/auth/whoami`.

### Ports
**8050** speaks the protocol Luna's `luna.ini` names, https or http. **8051** is plain HTTP on every address, for nodes; a password or token sent there crosses the network in clear text.

### Errors
A refusal or a failure answers its status and `{"message": "..."}` saying why: 400 a request that cannot be acted on, 401 no token or a bad one, 403 a role below the route's minimum, 404 no such object, 409 a conflict, 422 a body that does not match its schema (FastAPI's `detail` list instead of `message`), 502 the service behind trixd failed, 503 not available on this controller.
info.title: TrinityX Daemon (trixd)

What trixd holds for every node, or for the nodes named in `nodes`, in the shape
Luna's own hardware-rules export answers, so alertx reads either. Each entry carries
the node, whether a rule file is held, the number of rules and, unless `detail=no`,
the rule file itself as `document`, as `GET /api/v1/prometheus/hw-rules/{node}`
answers it. A node asked for and not held is listed with `exists: false`.

**Access:** reader or above: reader, operator, manager and rootus

patch.description:
Several nodes in one call, as alertx's save-nodes sends it. Each entry names a `node`
and any of `force`, `nhc` and `disabled`, which mean what they mean for one node in
`PATCH /api/v1/prometheus/hw-rules/{node}`.

Each node gets its own answer: `ok: false` with a `message` for a node Luna does not
know, or whose file could not be written, without stopping the others. Prometheus is
reloaded once for the lot, and not at all when nothing changed.

**Access:** manager or above: manager and rootus

get.description:
The Prometheus rule file trixd holds for one node, as YAML loads it: one group,
`trinityx_hw`, with one `MissingHardwareComponent` alert for each part `lshw` reported
when the file was generated. An alert fires when its part stops being reported, so a
missing DIMM, disk or card is noticed.

Each rule's labels say how its alert counts: `nhc`, whether it counts for the node's
health check, and `disabled`, whether it fires at all. A manager changes them with
`PATCH /api/v1/prometheus/hw-rules`.

**Access:** reader or above: reader, operator, manager and rootus

patch.description:
Called by the node itself after boot, by alertx's hook, with a node token for that
node from `POST /api/v1/auth/node/{node}`. trixd asks Prometheus which parts `lshw`
reports for the node and writes one alert for each.

A node that already has a rule file keeps it, so a reboot writes nothing and reloads
nothing; send `force: true` to generate the file afresh. `nhc` and `disabled`, when
sent, are set on every rule. Prometheus is reloaded only when the file changed, so a
thousand nodes booting at once cost a handful of reloads.

**Access:** a node token for the node in the path, from `POST /api/v1/auth/node/{node}`
